description: SABOCA, the Submillimetre APEX Bolometer Camera, was a 37-bolometer receiver on APEX for wavelengths around 350 micrometres. ESO lists a wavelength coverage of 352 μm. It was commissioned in 2009 and decommissioned in 2012.
facility_description: The Atacama Pathfinder Experiment is a 12-metre telescope at 5100 metres on the Chajnantor plateau in Chile, a project of the Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy hosted by ALMA.
notes: NJM's only band key is 852GHz. The ESO instrument page says SABOCA observed wavelengths of around 350 micrometres and lists wavelength coverage 352 μm. The ESO public page does not print 852 GHz. A Messenger PDF opened in this session contains the words 852 GHz (352 μm), about 120 GHz wide in a broken text extraction, and it does not print an ADS bibcode. That PDF's public URL was not confirmed, so 852GHz has no Description field. bibcode:2010Msngr.139...20S did not resolve. The APEX acknowledgement is required for APEX observational data and keeps the programme-ID placeholders. It was not shown to cover a filter curve. The ESO archive CC BY 4.0 grant is for data files. The public copyright page excludes scientific papers and other site text. No numeric transmission table was found, so redistribution of the curve is unknown. No magnitude system is stated.
